name: RoboBench
description: A comprehensive benchmark for evaluating multimodal large language models as embodied brains for robotic manipulation across five dimensions: instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis. It covers 14 capabilities, 25 tasks, and 6092 QA pairs, using data from large-scale real robotic datasets and curated in-house collection.
creator: Yulin Luo, Chun-Kai Fan, Menghang Dong, Jiayu Shi, Mengdi Zhao, Bo-Wen Zhang, Cheng Chi, Jiaming Liu, Gaole Dai, Rongyu Zhang, Ruichuan An, Kun Wu, Zhengping Che, Shaoxuan Xie, Guocai Yao, Zhongxia Zhao, Pengwei Wang, Guang Liu, Zhongyuan Wang, Tiejun Huang, Shanghang Zhang
rai:dataCollection: To evaluate five cognitive dimensions, the benchmark is built from open-source and in-house robotic data, enriched with MLLM- and human-provided annotations. Instruction comprehension uses paired explicit and implicit instructions, where explicit instructions are drawn from daily-life scenarios and implicit instructions are rewritten from them using LLMs. Perception reasoning datasets are constructed across robotic-centric, object-centric, scene-centric, and task-centric aspects using real robot data, curated attributes, GPT-generated functional properties and distractors, Gemini-segmented video steps, manual annotations, and human-labeled bounding boxes. Generalized planning is built from high-quality robotic videos, extracting frame sequences as standardized inputs. Affordance prediction samples representative frames from the planning pool and annotates static, dynamic, and mobile affordances. Failure analysis collects execution-level failures from RoboMIND and synthesizes planning-level failures by perturbing correct instructions.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Document analysis, Others
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Open-source and in-house robotic data; large-scale real-world robotic datasets; high-quality robotic videos; real robot data with type and view metadata; representative frames sampled from the planning pool; execution-level failures collected from RoboMIND.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Planning-level failures are synthesized by perturbing correct instructions, including wrong object, missing step, and wrong order. Explicit instructions are rewritten into implicit instructions using LLMs. For planning, natural language step descriptions are mapped into predefined function templates and instantiated with object references.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Frame sequences are extracted from robotic videos as standardized inputs. Data are standardized into multiple-choice QA for perception tasks. A two-stage quality control process is used: data filtering during construction and post-construction validation. General criteria address image quality and task validity, while sub-benchmarks have tailored rules such as excluding single-arm data from dual-arm tasks. After construction, 20 professionally trained annotators inspect linguistic clarity, answerability, and correctness. A majority-vote strategy is used: items all models solve correctly are removed, and items all models fail undergo manual review and correction.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations are provided by MLLMs and humans depending on the subtask. For perception reasoning, GPT generates functional properties and distractors; Gemini segments video steps for temporal grounding; manual annotations provide relative positions and keypoint changes; humans label bounding boxes linking instructions to target objects. For planning, Gemini generates structured annotations including task summaries, step-wise instructions with timestamps, and metadata such as objects, actions, scenes, and embodiments, which are refined by human annotators. For affordance prediction, representative frames are annotated with static contact points, dynamic motion trajectories, and mobile base positions. For failure analysis, execution-level failures are labeled by experts.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: After construction, 20 professionally trained annotators conduct comprehensive quality inspections validating linguistic clarity, answerability, and correctness. A majority-vote strategy is adopted: items that all models solve correctly are removed, whereas items all models fail to solve undergo manual review and correction.
rai:annotatorDemographics: 20 professionally trained annotators; expert annotators with prior training; experts labeled execution-level failures.
rai:dataSocialImpact: RoboBench is intended to provide a unified scaffold for measuring embodied cognition, clarify the role of the embodied brain, and guide the development of next-generation MLLMs toward more robust robotic intelligence.
rai:dataBiases: The authors note that current planning data primarily focuses on concrete action execution without explicitly distinguishing between left-right arm assignments or positional movements, which may contribute to failures in dual-arm coordination and mobile manipulation. They also note that performance drops on uncommon objects, symbolic reasoning, or world knowledge, suggesting weak integration of heterogeneous information.
rai:dataLimitations: The paper reports several benchmark-exposed limitations of current MLLMs: severe degradation on implicit instructions, weak robot-view recognition and temporal grounding, poor dual-arm coordination and rare-object reasoning, shallow affordance prediction, and difficulty with execution-level failure diagnosis. The authors also state that planning-level failures are synthesized due to lack of real-world planning failure data. Execution-level failure diagnosis is intrinsically difficult, with even human evaluators achieving relatively low scores.
rai:dataUseCases: The benchmark is designed for systematic evaluation of multimodal large language models as embodied brains for robotic manipulation. It supports evaluation across instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis, and is used to benchmark state-of-the-art MLLMs and establish a leaderboard.
